land.text: Syria, which Mu'awiya governed for the Rashidun caliphs from 639, taken out of Ali's caliphate in 656; the rest of the caliphate passed to him in 661

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Umayyad row starts 656 with Syria; the Rashidun shape of 661 is added by the 661 gain event.

land.text: the eastern and central lands taken in the revolution of 747-750: Khorasan, Iran, Iraq, Syria and Egypt

successors.note: Abbasid Revolution: Merv Feb 748, Kufa Sept 749, Damascus April 750, Egypt August 750.

land.text: Ifriqiya, held by the Fihrid emirate

successors.note: The Fihrid break-away is dated 745 by the Fihrids dossier (af-02); none of the nine pages here dates it.

land.text: al-Andalus, where the Umayyad prince Abd al-Rahman I 'proclaimed himself emir' in 756

successors.note: A different state from the caliphate (Cliopatria mislabels 751-756 as Umayyad Caliphate).

capitals.name: Damascus
capitals.note: Infobox: Damascus 661-744; for 656-660 it is Mu'awiya's seat as governor, which the page does not state. Hisham 'established his court at Resafa' in northern Syria (724-743, no year).

capitals.name: Harran
capitals.note: Infobox Harran 744-750, after Marwan II entered Damascus in December 744.

rulers.name: Mu'awiya I
rulers.title: governor of Syria 656-660, caliph from 661
rulers.note: Governor of Syria from 639; caliph from 661.

rulers.name: Abd al-Malik
rulers.note: The page gives the accession 'from 685' and no end year; 705 is al-Walid I's accession.

correction.text: Mu'awiya's Syria with Cyprus, the Cliopatria shape unchanged, for 656-657 only; Egypt joins in 658

keyframe_review.note: Syria (Levant 81%, Cyprus) is right for 656-657: 'Mu'awiya held Syria and, from 658, Egypt'. The Cliopatria Rashidun shape of 656-660 keeps Egypt, which is wrong from 658; the next keyframe adds it.

correction.text: Syria and Egypt: 'Mu'awiya held Syria and, from 658, Egypt'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from mid-658 Mu'awiya holds Egypt as well ('the Umayyad annexation of Egypt took place in 658'); Ali's Iraq, Arabia and Iran stay with Ali until 661.

correction.text: the whole caliphate under Mu'awiya: his Syria and Egypt plus the Rashidun shape of 661 (Arabia, Iraq, Iran) and Cyrenaica and Tripolitania, which the Rashidun dossier gains in 643

keyframe_review.note: The Cliopatria shape (Syria and Egypt, 0.92 M km2) stops at the 658 holdings, but from 661 Mu'awiya is caliph over everything: Ali was killed in January 661 and Hasan ceded the caliphate. Cliopatria carries the rest as 'Rashidun Caliphate' to 665 (Rashidun dossier: wrong after 661) and merges it only in 666. Corrected to the union of both shapes. Libya added (review of 2026-10-19): Cliopatria's 656-665 shapes have none although the Rashidun ledger gains Cyrenaica and Tripolitania in 643 and the 666 shape holds Cyrenaica.

6.93 M km2: Arabia, Syria, Egypt, Iraq, Iran and Khorasan. The Transoxiana page puts the border at the Oxus after 651. Not checked against any page: the Afghan part (60% of Afghanistan) and the Kabul valley fighting of 665-673, which the Turk Shahi dossier covers and no page I opened mentions. The shape lacks the Fezzan (666-667 raids, ledger). Adjusted (review of 2026-10-19): the shape's west edge is at 18.8 E and does not reach Germa (12.9 E), which the 666 gain takes from the Garamantes; the Fezzan is added as Cliopatria draws it from 692, with Libya. The Maghreb page does not say whether the Fezzan was kept.

correction.text: 666: the 666 shape plus the Fezzan (Waddan and Germa) and Cyrenaica and Tripolitania

keyframe_review.note: 7.0 M km2: adds Kairouan and the Tunisian interior, matching 'in 670 Uqba ibn Nafi founded Qayrawan'. Bukhara pays tribute from 674 (ledger) but is outside the shape. Fezzan and Libya added to stay with the 666 keyframe (they are held to the loss events of 690 and 698).

correction.text: 674-681: the 674 shape plus the Fezzan and Libya
682-683, to Yazid I's death in November 683: the caliphate as in 674

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 5.84 M km2 shape has holes in Syria (30%), Iraq (41%) and no Egypt, as in the civil war. But Yazid I reigned to November 683 over the whole caliphate and Ibn al-Zubayr was 'openly proclaimed caliph' only after Yazid's death. So 682-683 is the 674 shape; the civil-war pattern belongs to 684-691. Span fixed in the fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): 'to' 683 added, as the text above says 682-683. Without it the compiler read the keyframe as 682-691 (the Cliopatria shape years) and unioned this whole 674 shape into the check of every keyframe of 684-690, which kept Iraq, the Hejaz, Iran, Transcaucasia and Khorasan in the state while the ledger and the 684-690 keyframes took them out.

correction.text: 684: the 674 shape without the Hejaz, Yemen, Iraq, Egypt, Iran outside Khorasan, the Jazira, Khorasan with Afghanistan, Transcaucasia and Kairouan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (replaces the 684-691 shape of Levant and Egypt only; review of 2026-10-19): 1.3 M km2 of Iran, the Jazira, Khorasan and the Afghan lands, Transcaucasia, eastern Arabia and Libya were dropped with no loss event; they now go to the events of 683-685 (Zubayrid provinces, Jazira, Ibn Khazim, Najdat, nobody). What is left is Syria, the Turkish and Cypriot margins, Libya, the Fezzan and the lands no page places (Makran, the Saudi and Emirati margins). Egypt joins in March 685.

correction.text: 685-687: as 684 plus Egypt, without Najd, Bahrain and Oman

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Egypt retaken by Marwan and Abd al-Aziz in March 685 (Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page; Umayyad page 'In 685'), Najda's state in Najd, Bahrain and Oman from 685. Kairouan is Kusaila's.

correction.text: 688-689: as 685-687 plus Kairouan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Zuhayr ibn Qays retakes Kairouan in 688/9 (Maghreb page).

correction.text: 690-691: as 688-689 without Cyrenaica

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'a Byzantine fleet landing in Cyrenaica in 690'; 'Barqa had fallen out of Muslim control'. Tripolitania is kept: the page says nothing of it. Iraq returns in October 691, which this keyframe does not show (the year takes the start state); the 692 keyframe does.

correction.text: 692: the 692 shape minus Morocco, Fars, Kerman, Caucasian Albania and Iberia, Cyrenaica, Najd, Bahrain, Oman, Yemen and Ta'if

keyframe_review.note: 8.61 M km2 for 692-704. Hejaz, Iraq and its dependencies, the Jazira and Khorasan return in 691-692 (ledger); the shape also contains Fars and Kerman (Azariqa until 698), Morocco (taken 708/9), Caucasian Albania and Iberia (gained 705), Cyrenaica (lost 690, regained 694 at confidence 1) and the Najdat lands (gained 693; Yemen and Ta'if too), which are taken out. Applies to 692; 693 and 694-697 follow. Span fixed in the fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): 'to' 692 added, as the text says 692 and the note 'Applies to 692; 693 and 694-697 follow'. It ran 692-704 by the Cliopatria shape years and was unioned into the checks of the 693, 694, 698 and 701 keyframes, which have their own spans. Not corrected: the shape draws the Algerian and Tunisian Maghreb beyond the Kairouan region (the lands of Kusaila's and the Kahina's Berber kingdoms) from 692, while the ledger gains Carthage in 698, Numidia in 701 and Altava in 708; the Muslim conquest of the Maghreb page dates those events and says nothing of an Umayyad Sahara, so the Saharan cells (Ouargla, Bechar, Ghardaia, El Bayadh, Adrar, about 1,700 in the 692 snap) stay as Cliopatria draws them.

correction.text: 693: the 692 shape minus Morocco, Fars, Kerman, Caucasian Albania and Iberia and Cyrenaica

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Najdat are defeated at Mushahhar in 693 and Najd, Bahrain, Oman, Yemen and Ta'if return.

correction.text: 694-697: the 692 shape minus Morocco, Fars, Kerman, Caucasian Albania and Iberia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cyrenaica regained (694, confidence 1). The shape still draws Ifriqiya before Carthage falls in 698 (Cliopatria; not corrected).

correction.text: 698-700: the 692 shape minus Morocco, the Kahina's Numidia and Aures, Caucasian Albania and Iberia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 698-700 after Carthage (698) and the defeat of the Azariqa (698). The Kahina holds Numidia and the line to Ghadames from 698 to her defeat (loss event of 698, gain c. 701); Morocco is still outside until 708/9; Caucasian Albania and Iberia join in 705.

correction.text: 701-704: the 692 shape minus Morocco, Caucasian Albania and Iberia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Kahina is defeated around 701 (Maghreb page) and her country returns.

8.71 M km2 for 705-709: Tangier and the Sus (708/9) arrive at the end of the span, so Morocco is drawn one to three years early; the frontier is soft. Bukhara (709) is outside the shape; the ledger carries it.

correction.text: the 710 shape plus what the ledger has gained by 710 and the shape lacks: Bukhara (709), Tokharistan south of the Oxus (705, 710) and Tangier and the Sus (708); Hispania, Sindh, Sogdia and Khwarazm come with the events of 711-714

keyframe_review.note: 8.71 M km2 for 710-717 has no Hispania and no Sindh although both are conquered by 713-714 (Guadalete 19 July 711, Merida 712, 'Sindh and Multan to 713'), and nothing of Transoxiana although Bukhara fell in 709 and Samarkand and Khwarazm in 711-712 (Umayyad Caliphate page). Added; the ledger steps give the years. Fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): the earlier union of Hispania, Sindh, Sogdia and Khwarezm is taken out of this check, because the ledger gains each of them later and the compiler checks a keyframe only in its first year: Guadalete 19 July 711 and Merida 'mid-summer 712' (Umayyad conquest of Hispania page, with the 712-714 losses in visigothic-kingdom handing the land over), Khwarazm 712, 'Sindh and Multan' 713 (Umayyad campaigns in India page: 'Arab conquest of Sindh during 711-713'). Added to match events 43, 44 and 40: Bukhoro (709), the Afghan part of Bactria (Balkh and Tokharistan south of the Oxus, 705 and 710) and Morocco without the Saharan provinces (708).

correction.text: the 718 shape plus Sogdia and Khwarazm

keyframe_review.note: 9.84 M km2. The infobox gives 15,000,000 km2 for 720 (the text puts the greatest extent under al-Walid I, 705-715): ratio 0.66, within a factor of two; part of the gap is Transoxiana, which the shape omits (0% of Sogdia). Adds Sogdia and Khwarazm; Narbonne falls in 720 (ledger).

correction.text: the 724 shape plus Sogdia and Khwarazm; Gujarat and Rajasthan come with the 725 gains (Junayd's conquests, 723-726)

keyframe_review.note: 9.85 M km2. Sogdia is missing although the Arabs hold Samarkand against the Turgesh (Day of Thirst 724, 'hardly managed to reach Samarkand'); Bukhara is lost 728-732 (ledger). Sindh partly lost under Tamim (726-731) and Septimania held to 759. Gujarat and Rajasthan added from Junayd's conquests (725 gain, confidence 2); they are lost by 743. Fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): Gujarat and Rajasthan taken out of this check. The Umayyad campaigns in India page dates Junayd's conquests only to 723-726 ('Junayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Murri (723-726) recaptured Sindh, conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan') and the ledger gains them in 725 (events 68 and 69); the check at 724 pulled them in a year early and met the maitraka-dynasty keyframe of 724 (26 cells of Rajasthan). The Cliopatria shape has 4 cells there.

correction.text: the 732 shape plus Sogdia, Khwarazm, Gujarat and Rajasthan

keyframe_review.note: 9.88 M km2, the maximum. 'By 732 ... Caliphal authority' is restored at Samarkand and Bukhara returns; the Khazar front closes at Derbent in 737 (Transcaucasia 64%). Adds Sogdia and Khwarazm; no North Caucasus. Gujarat and Rajasthan are still held until 743 (ledger).

correction.text: 741-742: the 741 shape minus Morocco; Sogdia, Gujarat and Rajasthan added

keyframe_review.note: 9.84 M km2 still holds Morocco (55%), lost in the Berber revolt of 740 (739 on the Umayyad Caliphate page), and Ifriqiya (98%) to 749 although the Fihrids rule it from 745 (ledger, confidence 1). The Abbasid Revolution takes Khorasan in 748 and Iraq in 749. Gujarat and Rajasthan are lost by 743 (next keyframe). Span fixed in the fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): 'to' 742 added, as the text says 741-742. It ran to 749 by the shape years and was unioned into the 743 check, which put Gujarat and Rajasthan back into the state at 743 after the ledger had released them (events 82 and 84, 'The Arabs lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743', Umayyad campaigns in India page) and made the 743 conflicts with maitraka-dynasty (Gujarat, 423 cells) and gurjara-pratihara-dynasty (Rajasthan, 295 cells). The 741 and 732 checks still draw Gujarat and Rajasthan as the ledger holds them; where the Maitraka and Pratihara keyframes claim the same cells the size rule gives them to the Indian states, which fits the page (the Arabs were 'decisively defeated at Navsari in 739'; 'Umayyad expansion restricted to Sindh').

correction.text: 743-747: the 741 shape minus Morocco and the middle Maghreb (Algeria outside Ifriqiya, lost 742); Sogdia added

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The Arabs lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743'; Ifriqiya goes in 745, Khorasan in 748, Iraq in 749 (ledger). Fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): the middle Maghreb (Algeria outside the Ifriqiya region) subtracted to follow the new 742 loss; left in the shape it was re-taken at 743 and carried to the 750 check as 3,687 cells with no holder to hand them to (Ouargla, Bechar, Ghardaia, El Bayadh, Adrar, Ash Shati'). Berber Revolt page: after the Tlemcen expulsion 'The frontline of the Berber revolt now leaped to the middle Maghreb'; Emirate of Tlemcen 'by 742'.

correction.text: 750: Syria, the Jazira and Egypt as the 741 shape draws it (Nile valley, Delta, Sinai coast), the lands Marwan II still held in 750

keyframe_review.note: 5.21 M km2 for 750 still holds Mesopotamia (85%) and Hispania (76%). Kufa fell on 2 September 749, Damascus in April and Marwan II died in Egypt in August 750; Iberia was not under Umayyad government (ledger). Corrected to Syria, the Jazira and Egypt until April/August 750. Fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): Egypt narrowed from the whole country (3,364 cells) to the part the 741 shape draws (2,008). The Western Desert (Al Wadi at Jadid, Matruh) and the Red Sea hills were in no keyframe after 661 and no event took them from anyone, so the check at 750 added 1,147 cells of desert as new land in the last year of the state. The Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Fihri page still gives 'Egypt fell to the Abbasids in the middle of 750'. Not corrected: Fezzan and Cyrenaica (Ash Shati', Al Jufrah, Ajdabiya, Al Butnan, about 900 cells) stay in the state to 750 because no page opened says who held them after the Berber revolt.

correction.text: 751-754: unchanged shape, but not this state; al-Andalus under the Fihrid governors

keyframe_review.note: The Umayyad Caliphate ended in 750 ('from 661 to 750'). The Iberian land of 751-754 (Spain, Portugal, France) is al-Andalus under a Fihrid emir, nominally Abbasid until 'southern Iberia became de jure and de facto independent from the Abbasid Caliphate' in 756. Draw it under the Fihrid governors of al-Andalus (no dossier yet), not as Umayyad.

correction.text: 755-756: unchanged shape, but al-Andalus then the Emirate of Cordoba, not the caliphate

keyframe_review.note: 755 is still Fihrid al-Andalus; in 756 Abd al-Rahman I 'proclaimed himself emir or malik', founding the Emirate of Cordoba, which Cliopatria starts in 757. Neither year is the Umayyad Caliphate.

region.text: Syria, which Mu'awiya had governed since 639; the Cliopatria row starts here

ledger.note: 656: Mu'awiya, governor of Syria, holds Syria against Ali after Uthman's murder. First Fitna page: Uthman killed 'in June 656', Ali's accession 'triggered the First Fitna'; 'Mu'awiya held Syria and, from 658, Egypt'. Umayyad Caliphate page: Mu'awiya was appointed governor of Syria in 639 under Umar. The page does not use the word 'founded'; the caliphate proper is dated 661 (rename event).

region.text: the front between Ali's Iraq and Mu'awiya's Syria, where the armies met at Siffin

ledger.note: 657: Ali and Mu'awiya fight at Siffin. 'The armies met in 657. Fighting began on Wednesday, 26 July' and an arbitration agreement followed on 2 August 657; the result was a stalemate. The page I read does not locate the battlefield, so the zone is the frontier between the two shapes, not a named place.

region.text: Egypt, 'the Umayyad annexation of Egypt'

ledger.note: 658: Mu'awiya annexes Egypt. 'In mid-658, Mu'awiya I intervened directly in Egypt'; Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr was executed and Amr ibn al-As reinstated as governor. Cliopatria keeps Egypt in the Rashidun shape to 660.

region.text: the Hejaz and Yemen, entered by Mu'awiya's general Busr ibn Abi Artat

ledger.note: 660: Busr's raid takes oaths at Medina and Mecca and goes on into Yemen. 'In 660, Busr then continued his expedition into Yemen'; Ali held 'the Hejaz and Yemen' until Busr's raids and Jariya later restored his authority in Yemen. Raid, not annexation; the month is not given.

region.text: the front between Ali's Iraq and Mu'awiya's Syria

ledger.note: 660: the two sides stop fighting. In letters of late 660 'both parties agreed to cease military campaigns'; Abu Ishaq's account has Ali keeping Iraq and Mu'awiya Syria. An exchange of letters, not a formal treaty.

region.text: the Hejaz and Yemen

ledger.note: 661: Hasan cedes the caliphate and the Hejaz and Yemen fall to Mu'awiya without further fighting: Hasan 'concluded a peace treaty with Mu'awiya', ceding the caliphate.

region.text: the rest of the caliphate: Arabia, Iraq and Iran, the lands of Ali and Hasan

ledger.note: 661: Ali is killed ('In January 661, while praying at the Great Mosque of Kufa') and Hasan, proclaimed at Kufa, cedes the caliphate; Mu'awiya holds the whole of it from 661. The page gives no month for the treaty. The region is the Cliopatria Rashidun shape of 661, my reading of 'the caliphate'.

661: Mu'awiya becomes caliph and the Syrian state becomes the Umayyad Caliphate. 'Mu'awiya became caliph after the First Fitna, following Ali's assassination in January 661'; 'Mu'awiya's recognition in Kufa is generally taken as the start of his caliphate'. Colour and dossier continue from the Syrian state of 656.
661: Damascus becomes the capital ('Damascus became the capital'; infobox Damascus 661-744). Before 661 it was Mu'awiya's seat as governor, which the page does not state.

region.text: the Fezzan: Waddan and Germa, taken by Uqba ibn Nafi

ledger.note: 666-667: Uqba ibn Nafi takes the Fezzan. 'Uqba returned to the Fezzan and took Waddan' (663) and 'was campaigning in Sirte, Fezzan - taking ancient Germa' with the 666/7 raids. The page does not name the Garamantes; that is the other dossier's reading.

region.text: the interior of Ifriqiya around Kairouan, where Uqba ibn Nafi founded the garrison city

ledger.note: 670: Uqba ibn Nafi founds Kairouan. 'In 670 Uqba ibn Nafi founded Qayrawan'; the Arab-Byzantine wars page: the Exarchate was 'gradually seized between 647 and 670' and Kairouan 'established as a base for further invasions'. The Byzantine coast, with Carthage, stayed Byzantine until 698.

region.text: Bukhara, which paid tribute after Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad's crossing of the Oxus

ledger.note: 674: Bukhara accepts Arab suzerainty. Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad reached Marw in autumn 673 and crossed the Oxus 'in the following spring' (674 is the reading of that sentence); 'Bukhara accepted some Arab suzerainty and agreed to pay a large silver tribute' of one million dirhams. In 676 Sa'id ibn Uthman took Samarkand 'after three days' on a raid, with no lasting hold.

region.text: Kairouan and the interior of Ifriqiya, entered by Kusaila after the disaster at Tahuda

ledger.note: 683: after Uqba fell at Tahuda near Biskra in 683 'Kusaila now held undisputed mastery over North Africa and marched to Kairouan in triumph' (the page's paragraph dates it 683; the same page also gives 682 for the battle). Raised from confidence 1 on the Kusaila page (2026-10-19); the Maghreb page, the earlier source, has Kusaila entering 'Qayrawan unopposed' without a year.

region.text: the Hejaz, Iraq, Egypt and Yemen, and the Iranian provinces that were dependencies of Basra and Kufa (Fars, Kerman, Jibal, Azerbaijan, Khuzestan, Isfahan, Sistan and the rest of the Iran of the 674 shape outside Khorasan)

ledger.note: 683: Ibn al-Zubayr is proclaimed caliph. He 'was openly proclaimed caliph' after Yazid's death in November 683; 'Iraq and Egypt recognized him soon after, and most provinces recognized Ibn al-Zubayr as caliph'. The Umayyad Caliphate page adds that Medina expelled the Umayyads and the Battle of al-Harra was fought the same year; the Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page (opened for the Zubayrid dossier) names 'Egypt, Kufa, Yemen' among the provinces that offered allegiance, which is where Yemen comes from. Widened (review of 2026-10-19): the Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page has 'Most of the Islamic provinces offered their allegiance', the Second Fitna page 'most provinces recognized Ibn al-Zubayr as caliph', coins in his name 'as far east as Fars and Kirman, both dependencies of Basra', and the Mukhtar page has Iraq 'and its dependencies including Arminiya, Adharbayjan, Jibal'. No page lists the Iranian provinces one by one: Fars and Kerman, Jibal and Azerbaijan are the pages' words, Khuzestan, Isfahan, Sistan and the rest of Iran outside Khorasan are my reading of 'dependencies of Iraq'. The 674 shape gave the Umayyads 1.3 M km2 of Iran; Khorasan goes separately to Abd Allah ibn Khazim (684), Armenia and the Caucasus to nobody (next event), the Jazira in August 684.

region.text: Armenia and the rest of Transcaucasia as the 674 shape draws it

ledger.note: Page silent on a date: no page opened says when Arab authority left Armenia and the Caucasus. The Arab-Byzantine wars page has Justinian II (685-695) agreeing with the Arabs on 'joint possession of Armenia, Iberia and Cyprus' and, in 692, the Muslims conquering 'almost all of Armenia' after Sebastopolis; the Muslim conquest of Armenia page has nothing between 661 and 705. So the 684-691 keyframe leaves the 674 shape's Transcaucasia out and the 692 and 705 gains stand; 683, the year of the Second Fitna, is my bridging.

region.text: northern Syria, where the Qaysi tribes backed Ibn al-Zubayr

ledger.note: Page silent on the date: the Qaysi tribes of northern Syria backed Ibn al-Zubayr while 'central and southern Syria remained loyal to the Umayyads' (Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page); placed with the proclamation (683), as zubayrid /ledger/2 does. It ends at Marj Rahit (August 684, below).

region.text: Khorasan with the Afghan lands of the 674 shape, governed by Abd Allah ibn Khazim

ledger.note: Summer 684: Salm appointed Abd Allah ibn Khazim al-Sulami to Khorasan; he 'recognized Ibn al-Zubayr but ruled with virtual independence' (Second Fitna page, no year for the recognition), a nominal Zubayrid governor 'between 684 and his death' (Ibn Khazim page). The Afghan part outside Khorasan and Sistan is drawn with Khorasan because the 674 shape has it and no other holder is named; Kabul was briefly Arab 684-685 (turk-shahis dossier, not mirrored here).

region.text: northern Syria, where the Qaysi tribes backed Ibn al-Zubayr

ledger.note: Aug 684: Marj Rahit. 'Marwan was acknowledged as caliph at Jabiya in June 684' and at Marj Rahit in August 684 'pro-Zubayrid Qays, under Dahhak, were crushed by Marwan's pro-Umayyad forces'. Re-typed from a gain of northern Syria (review of 2026-10-19): the zubayrid-caliphate dossier has only the contest (its /ledger/2 and /6), the land was not handed over, and it is Umayyad in the 684 keyframe either way.

region.text: the Jazira, where the Qaysi survivors of Marj Rahit kept Ibn al-Zubayr's suzerainty

ledger.note: Aug 684: after Marj Rahit 'The surviving Qaysis fled to the Jazira under Zufar ibn al-Harith al-Kilabi, who continued to recognize Ibn al-Zubayr's suzerainty'; the Second Fitna page: the Qays 'continued supporting the Zubayrids'. The page gives no extent, so the whole Jazira region is drawn; Abd al-Malik besieged the Qaysite stronghold of Qarqisiya in 691 (Second Fitna page).

region.text: Egypt, regained from the Zubayrids

ledger.note: 685: Marwan I and his son Abd al-Aziz retake Egypt. Umayyad Caliphate page: Marwan I died in April 685 and 'his son Abd al-Aziz was appointed governor of Egypt'; the Second Fitna page: they 'expelled the Zubayrid governor of Egypt' during Marwan's caliphate (June 684 to April 685). Two pages give other dates: the Maghreb page 'In late 684', the Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr page (opened for the Zubayrid dossier) 'in March 685, Ibn al-Zubayr lost ... Egypt to Marwan'. 685 is where the two Zubayrid and Umayyad dossiers meet.

region.text: Najd and the Yamama, where Najda founded his Kharijite state

ledger.note: 685: Najda 'established an independent state in Najd and Yamama in 685' (Second Fitna page); the Najdat page dates his revolt there to 682 and does not say the land was taken from anyone. Mirror of najdat /ledger/0.

region.text: Bahrain (Eastern Arabia) and Oman, which the Najdat held

ledger.note: Page silent on when: the Najdat 'extended their authority to Bahrain, Oman, and parts of Yemen' (Second Fitna page, undated; the Najdat page does not mention Oman). Placed with the foundation (685), as najdat /ledger/1 does.

region.text: Kairouan and the interior of Ifriqiya, retaken from Kusaila's kingdom

ledger.note: 688/9: Zuhayr ibn Qays retakes Kairouan. 'In 688/9, Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan had consolidated enough to send Zuhayr ibn Qays to defeat Kusaila'.

region.text: Cyprus, held jointly with the Byzantine emperor

ledger.note: 688: 'In 688, the emperor Justinian II and the caliph Abd al-Malik reached an unprecedented agreement'; 'for the next 300 years, Cyprus was ruled jointly by both the Caliphate and the Byzantines as a condominium' and 'The collected taxes were divided between the Arabs and the emperor'. Raised from confidence 1 on the Cyprus in the Middle Ages page (2026-10-19). The Arab-Byzantine wars page adds Armenia and Iberia to the joint possession (Justinian II's first reign, 685-695) without a year.

region.text: Cyrenaica (Barqa), lost when a Byzantine fleet landed

ledger.note: 690: Byzantine landing in Cyrenaica. 'A Byzantine fleet landing in Cyrenaica in 690'; Zuhayr ibn Qays was 'defeated and slain by the Byzantines in Cyrenaica'; 'Barqa had fallen out of Muslim control' for the first time since Amr ibn al-As conquered it 'half a century earlier'.

region.text: Iraq retaken after the Battle of Maskin, with its dependencies in the Iranian north-west, south and east (Fars and Kerman stay with the Azariqa)

ledger.note: 691: Abd al-Malik reconquers Iraq. Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr 'was killed at the Battle of Maskin in October 691'; 'Abd al-Malik reconquered Iraq after the Battle of Maskin'. Widened (review of 2026-10-19) to mirror the 683 loss: 'Abd al-Malik then secured Iraq and most of its dependencies' (Second Fitna page, as read on 2026-10-19). The dependencies are the pages' 'Adharbayjan, Jibal' and my reading for the rest (confidence 2 for the event, 3 for Iraq alone). Mukhtar's north-west (Media, Azerbaijan) had passed back to Mus'ab in April 687.

region.text: the Jazira, where Abd al-Malik besieged the Qaysite stronghold of Qarqisiya

ledger.note: 691: 'In 691, he besieged the Qaysite stronghold of Qarqisiya in the Jazira'. The page does not say when the siege ended or when Zufar submitted, so 691 is my bridging for the Jazira's return, with Iraq.

region.text: Khorasan with the Afghan lands of the 674 shape, held by Abd Allah ibn Khazim with 'virtual independence'

ledger.note: 692: 'At some time before the end of 692, Ibn Khazim was intercepted and killed by Bukayr ibn Wisha al-Sa'di's troops', and Bukayr sent his head to Abd al-Malik; Bukayr succeeded him. The Second Fitna page has him killed in 691, the Ibn Khazim page 692 (used). Counterpart changed from the Zubayrid state to Ibn Khazim himself, whom the Zubayrids had as a vassal (review of 2026-10-19).

region.text: almost all of Armenia, after the Battle of Sebastopolis

ledger.note: 692: Sebastopolis. 'In 692, after the disastrous Battle of Sebastopolis, the Muslims invaded and conquered almost all of Armenia.' The Umayyad Caliphate page also has 'Umayyads defeated the Byzantines at Sebastopolis' in 692.

region.text: the Hejaz without Ta'if: Mecca, besieged by al-Hajjaj from March 692, and Medina

ledger.note: 692: Ibn al-Zubayr falls. Al-Hajjaj 'besieged Mecca from March 692'; Ibn al-Zubayr 'was killed in October/November 692, and the Hejaz came under Umayyad control'. The Second Fitna ends. Ta'if, held by the Najdat since 689, is gained in 693 (next events).

region.text: Najd and the Yamama, Bahrain, Oman, Yemen and Ta'if, held by Najda's Kharijite state

ledger.note: 693: the Najdat 'were eventually defeated by the caliphate in 693, at the battle of Mushahhar' (Najdat page, 2026-10-19; the page also has Najda murdered by Abu Fudayk in 691). Raised from confidence 1 and Ta'if added (review of 2026-10-19); the page names no lands, so the extent is the Najdat dossier's (najdat /ledger/5).

region.text: Cyrenaica (Barqa), regained from the Byzantines

ledger.note: Year not on any page: the Maghreb page has Barqa 'fallen out of Muslim control' in 690 and, 'In 694 a new army was sent, taking Carthage'; it never says who recovered Barqa. The Hassan ibn al-Nu'man page has 'the Byzantines' capture of Barce in Cyrenaica in c. 688' and his arrival in 692/93, 693/94 or 695; the Dihya page has him, defeated at Meskiana in 698, 'remained in Cyrenaica for five years', so it was Muslim by then. 694, the year of the new army, is my bridging; byzantine-empire has no 690 gain or 694 loss of Cyrenaica (eu-05).

region.text: Carthage and the Byzantine province of Africa, the Exarchate

ledger.note: 695: Hassan ibn al-Nu'man's campaign. 'They conquered and destroyed the Byzantine stronghold of Carthage between 695 and 698'; the Maghreb page: 'In 694 a new army was sent'; Hassan 'entered Carthage unopposed in 695/6'.

region.text: Carthage and the Byzantine province of Africa

ledger.note: 698: Carthage falls. 'Carthage was captured and destroyed'; the Maghreb page: 'ending the Byzantine presence by 698'.

region.text: Carthage and the Byzantine province of Africa

ledger.note: 698: the fighting for Carthage ends with its capture (Umayyad Caliphate page: 698).

region.text: Fars and Kerman, held by the Azariqa Kharijites

ledger.note: 698: al-Muhallab defeats Qatari. The Azariqa 'captured Fars and Kirman from the Zubayrids in 685'; Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a 'held parts of Fars and Kirman until al-Muhallab defeated him in 698'. The Azariqa stayed active in Iraq until suppressed in 696-699.

region.text: Numidia and the line from the Aures to Ghadames, the Kahina's state

ledger.note: 698-703: 'For five years Al-Kahina ruled a sovereign Berber state from the Aurès Mountains to the oasis of Ghadames (698-703)'; in 698 she demolished Baghaya, met Hassan in the Meskiana valley and 'defeated Hassan decisively'. The page dates the battle itself nowhere (the 698 is the sentence before it); mirror of kingdom-of-the-aures /ledger/5. Her fall: the Maghreb page 'around 701' (used for the gain below), the Hassan page 701, 702 or 703, the Dihya page 703 (Ramadan, El Jem).

region.text: Numidia and the Aures, the Kahina's country

ledger.note: c. 701: the Kahina is defeated. She was 'based in the eastern Aures' and met her defeat 'in a battle around 701'; the page does not give 698 or 703.

region.text: Lower Tokharistan: Balkh, 'recovered' by Qutayba ibn Muslim

ledger.note: 705: Qutayba takes Balkh. 'Qutayba began his tenure by recovering Balkh in spring 705, thereby bringing Lower Tokharistan to heel.'

region.text: Caucasian Albania and Iberia, combined with Armenia into the province of Arminiya

ledger.note: 705: Arminiya. 'Armenia, Caucasian Albania, and Iberia were combined into the province of Arminiya'; the Khazar wars page: from 705 they 'came under direct Arab rule as the province of Arminiya'. Armenian and Albanian princes kept local rule (in 732 Ashot III Bagratuni was made presiding prince of Armenia); the counterpart slug is the only Cliopatria polity of the three. Armenia itself is left out of this gain (review of 2026-10-19): it was gained from Byzantium in 692 (the event above) and nothing in the ledger loses it before 705.

region.text: Morocco: Tangier and the Sus, taken by Musa ibn Nusayr (without the Saharan provinces)

ledger.note: 708/9: Musa ibn Nusayr conquers Tangier and the Sus (page: '708/709'); the Maghreb page: 'In 708 after establishing a garrison at Tangier'; 'As late as 736 campaigns were still being sent into the Sus'. The land was held by Berber tribes, not a state. Fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): the region was the whole of Morocco as the gazetteer draws it, which includes the former Spanish Sahara provinces (Guelmim - Es-Semara, Laayoune - Boujdour - Sakia El Hamra, Oued el Dahab; 907 cells with Guelmim). The Muslim conquest of the Maghreb page: Musa 'personally conquered Tangier, then proceeded to campaign in the Sus al-Adna, before advancing to the Draa valley and the oasis of Tafilalt on the edge of the Sahara'; it never says the Sahara was taken, and the campaigns 'to the far south, into the Sus al-Aqsa' have no reported result.

region.text: Altava and its surroundings, the kingdom's core

ledger.note: 708: infobox 'Annexed by Umayyad Caliphate: 708' (the body gives no year; the page's last ruler 'died in the year 690 AD fighting against the Muslim conquest'). Mirror of kingdom-of-altava /ledger/7.

region.text: Bukhara, no longer a tributary

ledger.note: 709: Qutayba storms Bukhara. 'The city was taken by storm, a tribute of 200,000 dirhams imposed, and an Arab garrison installed in the citadel' after 'the long and bloody conquest of the kingdom of Bukhara' (706-709). The tributary becomes a garrisoned conquest.

region.text: Bukhara and its oasis

ledger.note: 709: Bukhara is annexed with an Arab garrison in the citadel (Transoxiana page).

region.text: Tokharistan south of the Oxus (Afghan Bactria), retaken after Nezak's revolt

ledger.note: 710: after Nezak's revolt of 709 'Abd al-Rahman retook Tokharistan' in spring and installed a garrison near Balkh; the page dates it only by sequence (710 is the reading). Fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): region narrowed from the whole gazetteer region Bactria, which also holds the Tajik Pamir, Khatlon and Uzbek Surkhandarya north of the Oxus, to its Afghan part, as the event text says 'south of the Oxus'. Muslim conquest of Transoxiana page: 'Come spring, Abd al-Rahman was able to re-establish Muslim control over Tokharistan almost without bloodshed.'

region.text: the Rif emirate as a client of the Caliphate

ledger.note: 710: 'The emirate was founded in 710 CE by Salih I ibn Mansur through a Caliphate grant'; infobox 'Client state of the Umayyad Caliphate (710-750)'. Mirror of emirate-of-nekor /ledger/1.

region.text: Baetica and the south, where Tariq ibn Ziyad landed

ledger.note: 711: Tariq lands. He 'departed from North Africa ... in early 711'; Roderic's army was 'utterly routed in the Battle of Guadalete' on 19 July 711.

region.text: Merida and Lusitania

ledger.note: 712: Merida. 'In 712, Tariq's forces were then reinforced by those of his superior' (Musa); Merida was 'ultimately conquered in mid-summer 712'. Cordoba and Toledo were 'stormed and captured unconditionally' (undated on the page).

region.text: Samarkand, the Sogdian principality

ledger.note: 711-712: Samarkand surrenders to Qutayba. The Umayyad Caliphate page dates the surrenders of Samarkand and Khwarazm to 711-712; the Transoxiana page gives no date for Samarkand's fall under Qutayba.

region.text: Khwarazm

ledger.note: 711-712: Khwarazm surrenders (Umayyad Caliphate page); the Transoxiana page is silent on a Qutayba conquest of Khwarazm.

region.text: the Ebro valley and the north: Zaragoza, Leon and Astorga

ledger.note: 713: Musa and Tariq meet and 'the following year the combined forces continued ... capturing Leon, Astorga and Zaragoza'. Theodemir 'conditionally surrendered' in 713 (the 'Treaty of Theodemir'); the page I read does not name his lands.

region.text: Sindh and Multan, taken by Muhammad ibn al-Qasim

ledger.note: 711-713: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim conquers Sindh. 'The conquest took place during 711-713'; the page's table dates 'the completion of the Arab conquest of Sindh and Multan to 713'. Sindh became a second-level province (iqlim). The Umayyad Caliphate page begins the campaign in 708/709. Dahir is named as ruler of Sindh; his death is undated.

region.text: Derbent (Bab al-Abwab), recovered by Maslama

ledger.note: 713/14: Maslama recovers Derbent. 'Maslama then recovered Derbent, which became a major Arab military outpost and colony'; the page gives 713/14 as the most likely date. Derbent had been taken in 642 (first Khazar war).

region.text: the Cantabrian mountains and the western Basque regions as far as Gallaecia

ledger.note: 714: Musa 'overran the western Basque regions and the Cantabrian mountains all the way to Gallaecia'; Pamplona's submission falls in this period without a date. The last Visigothic king, Ardo, took over from Achila II in 713 or 714.

region.text: the peninsula, conquered 'within five years' of 711

ledger.note: 714: the main conquest ends. 'Most of Hispania' was conquered within five years of Tariq's invasion of 711 (Umayyad Caliphate page); Musa reached Gallaecia in 714 (Hispania page). Septimania is a separate contest from 717.

region.text: the Sindh interior: Alor and Mehran, recaptured after Ibn al-Qasim's recall

ledger.note: 715: 'Indian kings recaptured most territories after Ibn al-Qasim left in 715' (Alor and Mehran in 715, renewed attacks at Brahmanabad in 718). Ibn al-Qasim was recalled in 715 and died on the way.

region.text: Jurjan (Gurgan) and Tabaristan

ledger.note: 716: Yazid ibn al-Muhallab invades. 'Yazid ibn al-Muhallab attempted to conquer Jurjan and Tabaristan.' The Dabuyid dossier carries the outcome (Farrukhan the Great contains the invasion).

region.text: Jurjan (Gurgan) and Tabaristan

ledger.note: 717: the page is silent on the outcome; the Farrukhan the Great page (opened for the Dabuyid dossier) has Yazid agreeing to withdraw 'in return for tribute' and 'The following year (717), the caliph Umar II had Yazid dismissed and imprisoned'. Tabaristan stayed Dabuyid.

region.text: Septimania, first raided across the Pyrenees by al-Hurr

ledger.note: 717: al-Hurr 'initiat[ed] in 717 the first forays across the Pyrenees into Septimania'.

region.text: Constantinople and the Marmara coast, besieged by land and sea

ledger.note: 717: the second siege of Constantinople. 'From July 717 to August 718, the city was besieged by land and sea by the Muslims.'

region.text: Constantinople and the Marmara coast

ledger.note: 718: the siege is abandoned ('the siege was abandoned on 15 August 718'). After 718 the border 'became stabilized along the mountains of eastern Anatolia', the Taurus-Antitaurus line.

region.text: Narbonne and its district

ledger.note: 720: Narbonne falls. The body says 'Narbonne fell (720)'; the timeline says Barcelona and Narbonne were captured 'by 719'. The Umayyad Caliphate page: Narbonne was conquered under Umar II and was the last stronghold in 759.

region.text: Sogdia, attacked by the Turgesh from 720

ledger.note: 720: the Turgesh counter-offensive. 'The Turgesh responded by launching a series of attacks against the Muslims in Transoxiana, beginning in 720.' In 721 Kul Chor defeated Sa'id ibn Abdu'l-Aziz near Samarkand.

region.text: Toulouse and Aquitaine

ledger.note: 721: Toulouse. An Umayyad army under Al-Samh was 'crushed by duke Odo's Aquitanian army at the Battle of Toulouse'; the Umayyad Caliphate page: 'Battle of Toulouse limited further expansion'.

region.text: Septimania

ledger.note: 721: the Visigothic kingdom ends; Ardo 'died in 721' and Septimania, its last land, is Umayyad (Narbonne 720).

region.text: Brahmanabad and the Sindh interior

ledger.note: 721: 'Hullishah surrendered at Brahmanabad'. Junayd, appointed governor of Sindh in 723, 'recaptured Sindh'.

region.text: the Derbent gate and the Albanian strip south of it, up to Balanjar

ledger.note: 722: the second Arab-Khazar war. In February-March 722 the Khazars 'decisively defeated the mostly Syrian army' at Marj al-Hijara; 'The Arabs broke through, storming [Balanjar] on 21 August 722'. In December 730 al-Jarrah's army was 'all but annihilated' at Ardabil and Khazar detachments reached Mosul.

region.text: Gujarat and Rajasthan, conquered by the governor Junayd

ledger.note: 723: Junayd (governor of Sindh from 723) 'conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan'; raids on Ujjain, Mirmad and Dahnaj ran 724-740; in 725 Nagabhata I 'defeated a large Arab force near Avanti'. Tamim (726-731) lost Junayd's gains; Al-Hakam (731-740) 'restored order in Sindh and Kutch'.

region.text: Gujarat and Saurashtra, conquered by Junayd

ledger.note: 723-726: 'Junayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Murri (723-726) recaptured Sindh, conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan'; 'Altogether, Al-Junayd have conquered all of Gujarat, a large part of Rajasthan, and some parts of Madhya Pradesh'; the kingdoms weakened or destroyed include the Maitrakas of Saurashtra, the Kacchelas of Kutch and the Gurjaras of Lata. The page gives no year inside 723-726; 725 is the middle, my bridging.

region.text: Rajasthan: Marmad, Bhinmal and Gurjaradesa, conquered by Junayd

ledger.note: 723-726: the same campaign took 'Mermad (Maru-Mada, in Jaisalmer and Jodhpur)', 'al-Baylaman (Bhillamala or Bhinmal)' and 'Jurz (Gurjaradesa)', destroying 'the Bhattis of Jaisalmer, the Gurjaras of Bhinmal, the Moris of Chittor, the Guhilas of Mewar'. Ujjain was raided and not conquered. The Gurjaras of Bhinmal are named as the nearest Gurjara state; the Pratihara dossier mirrors only the 738-743 contest.

region.text: Bukhara, taken by the Turgesh khagan Suluk

ledger.note: 728: 'Suluk, who in 728 took Bukhara'. From 728 to 732 the Turgesh controlled Sogdiana and the Ferghana Valley.

region.text: Bukhara and Samarkand, restored to the Caliphate at heavy cost

ledger.note: 732: 'By 732, two large Arab expeditions to Samarkand managed to restore Caliphal authority there, at heavy cost. Suluk then gave up Bukhara and withdrew north.'

region.text: Toulouse and Aquitaine

ledger.note: 732: the Umayyad advance into Gaul ends with the 'Umayyad defeat at Tours by the Franks'. Narbonne and Septimania stay Umayyad.

region.text: Balkh and Merv, seized by the rebel al-Harith ibn Surayj

ledger.note: 734: 'al-Harith ibn Surayj took Balkh and Marv, then defected to the Turgesh'. The page does not give the date of his defeat; in winter 737 he 'was defeated by the Umayyad governor Asad at the Battle of Kharistan'.

region.text: Balkh and Merv

ledger.note: 737 (winter): al-Harith is beaten at Kharistan by the governor Asad; the zone returns to the Caliphate.

region.text: the Derbent gate and the Albanian strip south of it

ledger.note: 737: Marwan ibn Muhammad's invasion ends the war. He advanced 'according to some Arab sources, to the Khazar capital of al-Bayda on the Volga' (a claim 'of little strategic value'); the result was 'establishing Derbent as the northernmost outpost of the Muslim world' and 'leaving the North Caucasus in Khazar hands'. The Umayyad Caliphate page: the Khazars 'were not subdued'.

region.text: southern Gujarat around Navsari, where the Arabs were defeated

ledger.note: 739: 'The Battle of Navsari (739): Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin defeated the Arabs.'

region.text: southern Gujarat around Navsari

ledger.note: 739: the Navsari fight is a single defeat; al-Hakam died in 740 fighting the Maitrakas.

region.text: Morocco, lost to the Great Berber Revolt

ledger.note: 740: 'In 740, Maysara al-Matghari' began the Berber revolt; 'By late 742 they'd annihilated several Arab armies'. The Umayyad Caliphate page dates the revolt to 739 and says Morocco 'would not again be ruled by an eastern caliph'. Cliopatria keeps Morocco in the Umayyad shape to 749.

region.text: the middle Maghreb: Algeria outside the Ifriqiya region (Tlemcen and the interior), lost to the Berber revolt

ledger.note: 742: the Great Berber Revolt reaches the middle Maghreb. Berber Revolt page: Tlemcen's Berber population drove out the Umayyad troops and 'The frontline of the Berber revolt now leaped to the middle Maghreb'; the Emirate of Tlemcen is dated 'by 742'; the Berbers 'managed to end Umayyad rule in the western Maghreb', while the core of Ifriqiya and Kairouan were saved (event of 745 below). The Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Fihri page: the western Maghreb 'remained out of his reach' and his attempts to reimpose his rule there failed. Added in the fx-05 pass (2026-11-01): the keyframes of 692-741 draw Cliopatria's Algeria as Umayyad and no event released it, so the 750 check found 3,687 Algerian and Saharan cells still held with nobody to hand them to. The year is the page's 'by 742' for the Tlemcen emirate; for the Saharan interior it is a bridging. The pages say nothing of Fezzan or Cyrenaica.

region.text: Transoxiana, recovered by Nasr ibn Sayyar

ledger.note: 743: 'Taking advantage of his [Suluk's] death, Nasr recovered most of Transoxiana by 743', 'except for the Ferghana Valley, control over which was lost'. Suluk was murdered by Kul-chor in 738 (inferred).

region.text: Sogdia

ledger.note: 743: the Turgesh war for Sogdia ends with Nasr's recovery of Transoxiana.

region.text: Rajasthan, the Arab conquests of Junayd

ledger.note: 743: 'The Arabs lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743.' Split by land (review of 2026-10-19): this is Rajasthan, which the 725 gain above took from the Gurjaras; Gujarat goes to the Maitrakas in the next event. Sindh stayed Arab, the only Umayyad area east of the Indus.

region.text: Gujarat and Rajasthan

ledger.note: 743: the Indian campaign ends; the page describes a hiatus from 740 to 750.

region.text: Gujarat and Saurashtra, the Arab conquests of Junayd

ledger.note: 743: 'The Arabs lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743'; the Arabs were 'decisively defeated at Navsari in 739'. Mirror of maitraka-dynasty /ledger/10.
744: Marwan II moves the capital to Harran. 'The capital was moved to Harran after Marwan II entered Damascus in December 744' (infobox Harran 744-750).

region.text: Ifriqiya, where Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Fihri proclaimed himself emir

ledger.note: 744-745: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib assembled a small force in Tunis and declared himself emir of Ifriqiya' (744); the Umayyad governor Handhala 'consented to return to Damascus in February 745'. The page adds that he sought confirmation from Marwan II, so the Umayyad overlordship became nominal; the land is drawn as lost from February 745, as the fihrids dossier has it. Raised from confidence 1 (2026-10-19).

region.text: Khorasan, where Abu Muslim raised the Black Standard

ledger.note: 747: 'On 9 June 747 (Ramadan 25, 129 AH), Abu Muslim successfully initiated an open revolt against Umayyad rule.' The Umayyad Caliphate page has Abu Muslim taking leadership in 746-747.

region.text: Khorasan

ledger.note: 748: Khorasan is won with the control of Merv on 14 February 748.

region.text: Khorasan: Merv, then Nishapur and the east

ledger.note: 748: 'On 14 February 748, he established control of Merv.' Nasr ibn Sayyar was driven out (expelled in 747 on the Umayyad Caliphate page) and 'died on 9 December 748 while trying to reach Hamadan'.

region.text: Rayy, which fell after the battle of Jurjan

ledger.note: Aug 748: Qahtaba 'defeated a 10,000-strong Umayyad force at the Battle of Jurjan in August and subsequently took Rayy' (Qahtaba page, 2026-10-19; the year is inferred from the page's February 748).

region.text: the Hamadan district: Nahavand, taken after Isfahan

ledger.note: 749: 'in March 749 he defeated a larger Umayyad army under Amir ibn Dubara ... near Isfahan'; 'Nihavand fell after a short siege and the Abbasid army began moving towards Iraq'. The page does not name Hamadan; the district stands for Nahavand. Replaces one event for Rayy, Hamadan and Nahavand at 748 (confidence 1).

region.text: Iraq, with Kufa

ledger.note: 749: Kufa falls on '2 September 749' and on 'Friday, 28 November 749' al-Saffah (Abu al-Abbas) is recognised as caliph in the mosque of Kufa. The page names Kufa only; Iraq is my reading.

region.text: Sindh, the only Umayyad area east of the Indus

ledger.note: Page silent on the date. The India page: Sindh was 'the only remaining Umayyad area east of the Indus' and describes a hiatus 740-750 'followed by civil war and the Umayyad collapse'; the Abbasid Revolution page is silent on Sind. Cliopatria's 750 shape no longer contains Sindh.

region.text: al-Andalus, governed by a Fihrid emir and not by the Abbasids until 756

ledger.note: 750: Yusuf al-Fihri, governor since January 747, was 'ruling independently following the collapse of the Umayyad Caliphate in 750' and 'ruled as king (malik), and not as governor (wali)' for nine years; Abd al-Rahman beat him at Musarah in March 756. The page does not say whether he recognized the Abbasids. Raised from confidence 1 (2026-10-19).

region.text: the Rif emirate

ledger.note: 750: the infobox range of the client status ends in 750; the page does not describe the end of the relation (mirror of emirate-of-nekor /ledger/2).

region.text: Syria, with Damascus

ledger.note: 750: the Zab ('On 16 January 750' the forces met and Marwan II was defeated 'nine days later') and then 'Damascus fell to the Abbasids in April'. The page gives no year in that sentence; the context is 750. The Umayyad Caliphate page: Umayyad revolts in Syria and on the Byzantine frontier were defeated late in 750.

region.text: Egypt, where Marwan II was run down

ledger.note: 750: 'In August, he and his family were tracked down and killed in Egypt.'

region.text: what remained of the caliphate in 750

ledger.note: 750: the Umayyad Caliphate ends with the death of Marwan II. The Abbasid Revolution page dates the revolution '9 June 747 - July 750'; the Umayyad Caliphate page: 'from 661 to 750'. An Umayyad prince, Abd al-Rahman I, founded an emirate at Cordoba in 756 (Cliopatria's Emirate of Cordoba row, a different state).

wars.name: First Fitna

zones.text: the front between Iraq and Syria (Siffin, 657)

wars.outcome: Mu'awiya won: Ali was killed in January 661, Hasan ceded the caliphate and Mu'awiya held the whole of it, with Egypt taken in 658.
wars.note: Control 658-660: Mu'awiya Syria and Egypt; Ali Iraq and, until Busr's raids, the Hejaz and Yemen.

wars.name: Second Fitna

zones.text: Kufa under Mukhtar Oct 685 - Apr 687, then Mus'ab; Maskin Oct 691
Najda's state in Najd and Yamama from 685

wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: the Zubayrid caliphate dissolved with Ibn al-Zubayr's death in October/November 692 and the Marwanids replaced the Sufyanids.
wars.note: The Kharijite states outlived the Zubayrids: Najda killed c. 691, the Azariqa beaten in 698.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of the Maghreb (Umayyad phase)

zones.text: Kairouan, founded 670, lost to Kusaila c. 683, retaken 688/9

wars.outcome: The Byzantines left Africa (Carthage 698), the Kahina fell c. 701 and Morocco was taken in 708/9; the Berber revolt of 740 lost Morocco again.

wars.name: Umayyad conquest of Hispania

zones.text: most of Hispania within five years

wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: the Visigothic kingdom ended (Ardo died 721), the north was left to the Asturian principality, and the advance stopped at Toulouse (721) and Tours (732).

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Transoxiana (Umayyad phase)
wars.outcome: Qutayba conquered 'the larger part of Transoxiana' in 705-715; the Turgesh took Bukhara in 728, the Arabs restored Samarkand by 732, Nasr recovered 'most of Transoxiana by 743', except the Ferghana Valley.
wars.note: The Battle of Talas (751) is Abbasid.

wars.name: Second Arab-Khazar war
wars.outcome: Stalemate: the Khazars beat the Arabs at Ardabil (730) but Marwan ibn Muhammad's 737 invasion left Derbent 'the northernmost outpost of the Muslim world' and the North Caucasus in Khazar hands.
wars.note: First war 642-652 is in the Rashidun dossier.

wars.name: Arab-Byzantine wars (Umayyad period)
wars.outcome: Arab gains in Armenia (692) and Africa (698); both sieges of Constantinople failed (678, 718); the frontier settled on the Taurus-Antitaurus line.
wars.note: The 674-678 siege was a Cyzicus-based blockade from 674 and a land siege from 676.

wars.name: Umayyad campaigns in India
wars.outcome: Victory of the Indian kingdoms: 'Umayyad expansion restricted to Sindh' (infobox 711-740).

wars.name: Abbasid Revolution
wars.outcome: Abbasid victory: 'Abbasid victory' (9 June 747 - July 750); the Zab was fought in January 750 and Marwan II killed in Egypt in August.

certainty.note: Civil war: which lands each side held is approximate and the Cliopatria shape is largely replaced by 658 and 684 keyframes.
Steppe, desert and Berber frontiers are approximate. The Derbent line after 737 and the Taurus-Antitaurus line after 718 are the firmest ('stabilized').

notes:
Written for group me-07 on 2026-10-19 from nine Wikipedia pages (budget 9). Dates come from the pages as WebFetch returned them; where two pages disagree the event cites one and the other is in the note (Berber revolt 739/740, Sindh 708/709 or 713, Cyprus 649/653).
Cliopatria problems: (1) 751-756 'Umayyad Caliphate' is al-Andalus (Fihrid emir, then the Emirate of Cordoba); marked wrong, needs a dossier 'Fihrid al-Andalus' (suggested slug fihrid-al-andalus, group eu-12). (2) 682-691 gives the Umayyads Arabia, Persia and Iraq they did not hold. (3) Rashidun shape 661-665 continues after Ali's death; the 661 keyframe merges it. (4) Transoxiana, Sindh to 718 and Hispania 710-717 are missing; Morocco is held 692-739 although conquered 708/9; Fars/Kerman held 692-697 although Azariqa. (5) Ifriqiya after 745 is Fihrid per the other dossier (not on my pages).
Start year: 656 is the Cliopatria year (Mu'awiya's Syria); the caliphate proper is 661 (rename). A reviewer who wants start 661 can move the found event; the 656-660 keyframes then become a Syrian state.
Not on the pages opened: Cilicia's date (permanently occupied under the late Umayyads), Ceuta (the Exarchate dossier dates it 709), Siffin's location, the 745 Fihrid break-away, the Kabul valley wars of 665-673 and 684-685, the Persian provinces as internal units (Khorasan, Iraq, Ifriqiya, Arminiya, al-Andalus, Sind have no dossier). The Khazar frontier appears as a contest zone only.
Gazetteer names used that may be missing: none of the standard ones; 'Rey' and 'Mary' are place names from places.jsonl. Counterparts without dossiers: zubayrid-caliphate, mukhtarid-state-of-kufa, najdat-kharijite-emirate, azariqa-kharijite-emirate (written by this group), Bukhara, Samarkand, Khwarazm, Hindu kings of Sindh, Dahir's kingdom of Sindh, Fihrid governors of al-Andalus, al-Harith ibn Surayj (names only).
Repair of 2026-10-19 (review me-07): the Second Fitna is now one accounting across the umayyad, zubayrid, mukhtarid, najdat and azariqa dossiers. The 683 loss to the Zubayrids covers the Hejaz, Iraq, Egypt, Yemen and the Iran of the 674 shape outside Khorasan; the Jazira goes in August 684 (Qays under Zufar), Khorasan with the Afghan lands to Abd Allah ibn Khazim (684), Nejd, Bahrain and Oman to the Najdat (685), Transcaucasia to nobody (683, confidence 1); Egypt returns in 685, Kairouan in 688, Cyrenaica is lost in 690 and regained in 694 (confidence 1), Iraq with its dependencies and the Jazira in 691, Khorasan in 692 (the Ibn Khazim page; the Second Fitna page says 691), Najd and the rest in 693. The keyframes 684-694 follow these events one by one. Gujarat and Rajasthan are gained c. 725 and lost in 743; Arminiya in 705 is Caucasian Albania and Iberia only; Altava 708, Nekor 710-750, the Kahina 698 and Ceuta (see below) are added or checked against the neighbours; Fezzan and Libya are in the keyframes from 661; Ta'if goes with the Najdat lands (693). Ceuta: the Maghreb page has Musa's advance 'checked by Count Julian' at Ceuta and the Visigoths taking it over after 698-702; its only 709 is the introduction's 'the Byzantine Empire lost its last remaining strongholds'. The exarchate-of-africa dissolve of Ceuta to the Umayyads in 709 is therefore not mirrored here. Open: the Cliopatria shapes still draw Ifriqiya before Carthage (698); the pages give no extent for the Iranian dependencies of Basra beyond Fars, Kerman, Jibal and Azerbaijan; Makran, Turkmenistan and the Saudi and Emirati margins of the 674 shape are left Umayyad by default in 684-691; Kabul 684-685 (turk-shahis) and the Constantinople sieges of 672-678 are not mirrored. Fix pass fx-05 (2026-11-01): keyframe spans of 682 (to 683), 692 (to 692) and 741 (to 742) set to the years their texts give; keyframes 710, 724, 743 and 750 and ledger events 40 and 44 narrowed to what the ledger and the pages support; ledger event 742 (loss of the middle Maghreb, Berber Revolt page) inserted before the 743 events, so ledger indices from 79 on are one higher than before. See history/polities/_notes/fix-fx-05.md.
